parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Alex the parrot was tested for comprehension using three response labels. Two of these were
colour and shape.
Name the third response label that Alex could use.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Alex the parrot had indirect experience of novel (new) objects before the Transfer Tests. This
was to reduce a fear response in Alex.
Outline the indirect experience Alex had with novel (new) objects before the Transfer Tests.

text: From the study by Pepperberg (parrot learning):
The study by Baron-Cohen et al. (eyes test) revised the ‘Reading the Mind in the Eyes’ test from
the original version.
Describe the original version of the ‘Reading the Mind in the Eyes’ test.
Explain one problem that could arise if children were used as participants in the study by Milgram
(obedience).

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Participants arrived at the laboratory before their usual bedtime.
Outline the procedure from when a participant arrived at the laboratory until the end of the
study.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Outline one conclusion from this study in relation to eye movement during REM sleep.

text: From the study by Dement and Kleitman (sleep and dreams):

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
One aim was to investigate whether chimpanzees only help when they can see what another
chimpanzee needs to complete a task.
Outline one other aim.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: The results included data from one ‘Cannot See’ condition and two ‘Can See’ conditions.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Outline one result from the ‘Cannot See’ condition.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Outline one result from the second ‘Can See’ condition.

text: From the study by Yamamoto et al. (chimpanzee helping):

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe the background to this study.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain why this study is from the cognitive approach.

text: From the study by Laney et al. (false memory):
Suggest two real-world applications based on the study by Bandura et al. (aggression).
Your suggestions must be ethical.
Two friends, Himmat and Urvi, are discussing the individual and situational explanations for
behaviour in relation to the study by Canli et al. (brain scans and emotions). Himmat thinks
the study supports the individual explanation but Urvi thinks the study supports the situational
explanation.
Explain one reason why Himmat is correct and one reason why Urvi is correct, using evidence
from this study.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe the sample used in the study by Piliavin et al. (subway Samaritans).

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Explain whether each ethical guideline below was broken in the study by Piliavin et al.
(subway Samaritans):
confidentiality ______
informed consent ______
protection from psychological harm ______
right to withdraw ______

text: Evaluate the study by Andrade (doodling) in terms of two strengths and two weaknesses. At least
one of your evaluation points must be about generalisations.
